identity.description: A single CART tree: recursive axis-aligned partitioning by impurity-minimizing threshold splits. The glass-box of the family — every prediction is a readable root-to-leaf rule path — at the cost of high variance that the ensemble siblings exist to average away. The value proposition is the explanation, not the accuracy ceiling.

emits.note: classification; the class fraction of the landing leaf — piecewise-constant and coarse (few distinct values), so calibrate before trusting the numbers
the fitted partition as readable predicates (export_text / tree_ structure) — the rule paths ARE the explanation; no external explainer needed

max_depth.note: the interpretability budget — depth d means at most d predicates per explanation; null grows to purity and memorizes

max_features.note: null (all features) is the right default for a single tree — subsampling features only helps when averaging many trees

ccp_alpha.note: cost-complexity (minimal cost-complexity) pruning — the principled way to trade leaves for generalization after growing

invariances.why: splits are threshold comparisons on single features; any monotone rescale yields the identical tree
the best-split search over order statistics depends only on feature ORDER; log/rank/box-cox cannot change the chosen partition
sklearn >=1.3 trees route missing values down the lower-impurity child for dense numeric input; a driver pinned below 1.3 must impute — version-gated, hence empirical
sklearn trees require numeric input; categoricals must be pre-encoded
a non-parametric partition makes no assumption about the marginal or error distribution
fits anywhere, but a single tree's variance grows with depth and large n does not buy accuracy past moderate depth — beyond that the family answer is a forest, not a deeper tree
piecewise-constant leaves; outside the training range the prediction clamps to the boundary leaf

featureStats.why: each split halves the rows available below it; low n relative to p exhausts the sample after a few levels, forcing shallow trees whose rules may be honest but weak
impurity gains vanish when one class dominates — leaves collapse to the majority label and the rule set reads as vacuously 'predict majority'
learned NaN routing (sklearn >=1.3) keeps rows in the partition, and the missing-direction branch itself becomes a readable rule ('X missing → left')

modelMetrics.why: an unpruned CART drives train error toward zero by construction (memorization); the train-vs-CV gap is the direct overfit read that sets max_depth/ccp_alpha
the number of leaves is the size of the rule set — the explanation budget; a 500-leaf tree has forfeited the Rules value proposition and should be a forest instead
quantifies the accuracy price paid for readability; a small gap justifies committing to the glass-box, a large one flags variance the single tree cannot shed

edgeCases.behavior: grows to purity and memorizes the training set (train score ~1.0)
structurally unstable — perturbing a few rows reshuffles the whole partition, so the 'explanation' is an artifact of the sample

edgeCases.condition: signal in a linear combination of features (rotated/oblique boundary)
edgeCases.behavior: axis-aligned splits approximate a diagonal with a staircase of many shallow rules
majority-class leaves everywhere; minority never earns a split
depth-1 stump with near-perfect score — the leakage signature

driver.wrapperNeeds: rules emission: serialize export_text(tree) / tree_ structure alongside predictions

canBeSeeds.note: the canonical base learner — bagging decision trees with per-split feature subsets recovers the random forest
leaf-fraction probabilities are coarse and overconfident at pure leaves

placementClaims.why: learned NaN routing (driver floor sklearn>=1.3) makes upstream imputation unnecessary, and the missing-branch rule is itself interpretable output
monotone-transform-invariant: log/Yeo-Johnson cannot change the chosen splits — though raw-unit thresholds read better in the emitted rules, which is a UI concern, not a fit concern

scale-insensitive by mechanism — the fit is unchanged; note standardization rewrites rule thresholds into z-units ('income > 0.73 SD'), hurting the readability of the emitted rules, so prefer raw units when this model is terminal
sklearn trees need categoricals encoded to numeric before fit
